reveal.answer: Mostly into heating the bulb and the room. A filament bulb turns less than 10% of its energy into light. The rest is dissipated.

learn.heading: Efficiency
learn.equation: efficiency = {useful output energy transfer/total input energy transfer}
learn.example: A radio uses 300 J and gives out 210 J of sound. Efficiency = 210 ÷ 300 = 0.70 = 70%.

build.q: A motor transfers 300 J usefully from 600 J. What is its efficiency?

build.q: Which efficiency is impossible?
build.explanation: Useful output can never be more than the input: energy cannot be created.

build.q: What is the unit of efficiency?
build.explanation: It is energy ÷ energy (or power ÷ power), so the units cancel.

build.q: A 100 W lamp is 0.10 efficient. What is its useful power output?
build.explanation: 0.10 × 100 = 10 W. The other 90 W is wasted.

In the kinetic store of the device

developing.a: efficiency = useful output energy transfer ÷ total input energy transfer

developing.a: Energy cannot be created, so the useful output can never be more than the input.

reaching.q: A transformer is supplied with 200 000 W and wastes 2000 W. Calculate its efficiency.
reaching.equation: efficiency = useful power output ÷ total power input

reaching.a: Less friction, so less energy is dissipated as heat. More of the input becomes useful output.

mastering.q: A 1.2 kW kettle heats 0.50 kg of water by 80 °C in 160 s. c = 4200 J/kg °C. Calculate its efficiency.
mastering.given: P = 1200 W, t = 160 s, m = 0.50 kg, c = 4200 J/kg °C, \Delta\theta = 80 °C
mastering.equation: E = P t; \Delta E = m c \Delta\theta; efficiency = useful ÷ total

mastering.q: (HT) Suggest three ways to increase the efficiency of a car.
mastering.a: Lubricate moving parts; streamline the body to cut air resistance; reduce its mass. Each cuts wasted energy.

mastering.q: A ball dropped from 1.0 m bounces back to 0.70 m. Calculate the efficiency of the bounce. Where did the rest go?
mastering.a: 0.70 ÷ 1.0 = 0.70 (70%). The rest was dissipated as thermal energy and sound.

build.q: What happens to the temperature of ice while it is melting?
build.explanation: The energy breaks bonds, so the temperature stays at 0 °C until all the ice has melted.

build.explanation: L = E ÷ m, so joules per kilogram. J/kg °C is specific heat capacity.

build.title: Demo: specific latent heat of ice
build.intro: Your teacher melts crushed ice with a heater and measures the energy supplied and the mass of water melted.
steps: Pack crushed ice around a heater in a funnel. Set up a second funnel of ice with no heater.
Stand a beaker under each funnel to collect the melted water.
Switch the heater on for a set time. Energy supplied = power × time.
Mass melted by the heater = heater beaker − control beaker. L = E ÷ m.
build.warning: Water and electricity: only the teacher handles the heater and power pack.
build.imageDescription: two funnels of crushed ice over beakers on balances, one containing an immersion heater

questions.q: Why is the ice crushed?
questions.a: So it touches the heater well and less energy is lost to the air.

questions.q: Why is the control funnel needed?
questions.a: Some ice melts from the warmth of the room. Subtracting it gives the mass melted by the heater alone.

questions.q: Calculate the energy to melt 3.0 kg of ice. L = 334 000 J/kg.

reaching.a: The energy breaks bonds between particles, raising their potential energy, not their kinetic energy. So the temperature stays constant.

reaching.q: What is the difference between the latent heat of fusion and of vaporisation?
reaching.a: Fusion: solid to liquid (melting or freezing). Vaporisation: liquid to gas (boiling or condensing).

mastering.q: 0.20 kg of ice at 0 °C melts, then warms to 20 °C. L = 334 000 J/kg, c = 4200 J/kg °C. Find the total energy.
mastering.given: m = 0.20 kg, L = 334 000 J/kg, c = 4200 J/kg °C, \Delta\theta = 20 °C
mastering.equation: E = m L, then \Delta E = m c \Delta\theta

mastering.q: Steam at 100 °C causes worse burns than water at 100 °C. Explain why.
mastering.a: Steam releases its latent heat of vaporisation as it condenses on the skin, a lot of energy, before cooling like the water.

mastering.q: In the demo, the value of L came out higher than 334 000 J/kg. Suggest why.
mastering.a: Some heater energy went into the air and funnel instead of melting ice, so the E used in L = E ÷ m was too big.

engage.hook: Your body has about 200 different kinds of cell. Why are they not all the same shape?
engage.imageDescription: drawings of different specialised cells: nerve, sperm, red blood, palisade, root hair

reveal.answer: Each kind does a different job, and its shape and parts suit that job. A nerve cell is long because it carries signals across the body.

items: A specialised cell has a structure adapted to its function.
Its shape and sub-cellular structures suit one job.
Cells become specialised by differentiation: they gain new sub-cellular structures.
Most animal cells differentiate early in life.
Many plant cells can differentiate throughout their life.

learn.heading: Specialised animal cells

items: Tail to swim to the egg.
Lots of mitochondria release energy for swimming.
Acrosome holds enzymes to digest into the egg.
Nerve: long axon carries impulses; branched ends connect to other cells.
Muscle: protein fibres contract; lots of mitochondria for energy.

learn.imageDescription: labelled diagrams of a sperm cell, a nerve cell and a muscle cell

learn.heading: Specialised plant cells

items: Long hair gives a large surface area to absorb water and mineral ions.
No chloroplasts: it is underground, with no light.
Xylem: dead cells, no end walls, strengthened by lignin. Carries water and minerals up.
Phloem: living cells joined by sieve plates. Carries dissolved sugars up and down.

learn.imageDescription: labelled diagrams of a root hair cell, xylem vessel and phloem tube

build.q: Why does a sperm cell have lots of mitochondria?
build.explanation: Mitochondria release energy by respiration, which powers the tail.

build.q: Which adaptation helps a root hair cell absorb water?
build.explanation: The long hair gives a large surface area for absorption.

build.q: What is differentiation?
options: Cells dividing to make more cells
A cell gaining structures for a special job
build.explanation: A differentiating cell gains new sub-cellular structures and becomes specialised.

build.q: Which cell carries electrical impulses?
build.explanation: Nerve cells carry impulses along their long axons.

build.q: Which tissue carries dissolved sugars around a plant?
build.explanation: Phloem carries sugars. Xylem carries water and minerals.

build.q: Why do xylem cells have no end walls?

build.explanation: Dead, hollow cells joined end to end make a tube for water.

statements.text: Another name for the egg cell is the ovum.
Muscle cells get longer when their fibres contract.
statements.correction: They get shorter when they contract.

statements.text: Palisade cells are found in the roots of plants.
statements.correction: They are in leaves, packed with chloroplasts.

statements.text: Root hair cells contain no chloroplasts.
Red blood cells contain chlorophyll to carry oxygen.
statements.correction: They contain haemoglobin, which carries oxygen.

developing.a: A cell whose structure is adapted to carry out a particular function.

reaching.q: Explain how a root hair cell is adapted to absorb water.

reaching.q: Explain why muscle cells contain many mitochondria.
reaching.a: Contracting needs a lot of energy. Mitochondria carry out respiration, which releases it.

reaching.q: Compare the structure and function of xylem and phloem.

mastering.q: A nerve cell can be 1 m long. Explain how its structure suits its function.
mastering.a: Its long axon carries impulses a long way quickly. Branched endings connect to many other cells.

build.title: Insulation and cooling
build.intro: Find out how the number of insulating layers affects how fast a can of hot water cools.
steps: Wrap each can in a different number of layers: 0, 1, 2 and 3.
Put the same volume of hot water in each can. Record the start temperature.
Record the temperature of each can after 10 minutes.
Work out the temperature drop for each can.
